title: 9 Questions to Ask a Heat Pump Installer Before You Sign
desc: Nine plain questions that show which heat pump installers know their stuff, protect your rebate and give a fair quote. Includes a 5-question quiz.
h1: 9 Questions That Make a Heat Pump Installer Sweat (In a Good Way)
lead: A good installer loves these questions. A weak one dodges them. Ask all nine before you sign, and you will know which is which.

image.alt: Two workers handling ductwork on a rooftop beside rows of outdoor air conditioning units

takeaways: Ask which program lists them, and check that list yourself.
Ask for the exact model and check it is on the rebate's qualified list.
Ask who files the rebate and when, in writing.
Get at least three quotes and compare the same things in each.
intro:
A heat pump is a big purchase, and the rebate rules are strict. A small mistake, like the wrong model or the wrong paperwork order, can cost you thousands. The company you pick matters as much as the machine.

You do not need to know HVAC to ask smart questions. Each one below has a plain reason behind it and a sign of a good answer. Our installer rankings list top-rated companies by Google reviews. Use these questions on the three you shortlist.
items: Are you on the program's official list?

Some rebates only pay when the work is done by a company the program recognizes. BC Hydro's heat pump rebate needs a member of the Heat Pump Contractor Network (HPCN), and the rebate page lists that rule. Ask for the company's membership and then check the official list yourself. Do not just take their word.

Good answer: a quick yes and a link or number you can look up.
How did you decide on the size?

A bigger unit is not a better unit. BC Hydro's whole-home rebate asks that the heat pump meets 100% of your heating at -5°C, and Ontario's program asks for sizing based on an approved method. Ask to see the heat loss math for your house, not a rule of thumb.

Good answer: they measured your home, or ask for details like insulation and windows.
What is the exact make and model?

Rebates pay for models on a qualified list, not for any heat pump. BC Hydro, for example, asks for a cold-climate model with specific efficiency ratings. Get the model numbers of the outdoor and indoor units in writing and compare them to the list.

Good answer: model numbers on the quote, plus the list they checked.
Who files the rebate, and when?

Ontario's heat pump stream says the contractor files within 30 days and the cheque comes within 60. In BC you apply within six months of the invoice date. Ask who does the filing, what you must sign and what happens if the program rejects it.

Good answer: a clear plan with dates.
Do I need approval before work starts?

In Ontario you need written pre-approval before the install, so you cannot apply after the fact. Ask the installer if they handle that step, and do not let work start until it is in your inbox.

Good answer: they explain the order of steps without being asked.
What will my electrical panel need?

Some homes need a bigger panel and some do not. Ask if they checked yours and if the quote includes any electrical work. A surprise panel bill is the most common change order.

Good answer: they looked at the panel during the visit.
Where will the outdoor unit go?

Ask about spots away from bedrooms and neighbours, snow, and drainage. We do not publish noise limits, because local rules vary, so ask your city or strata about them too.

Good answer: they walked the property and gave a reason for the spot.
What does the payment schedule look like?

Ask how much is due up front, what is due at each step and what happens if a rebate is denied. Compare it with the deposit rules in your province. Never pay the full price before the work is done.

Good answer: a written schedule tied to steps, not dates alone.
What does the warranty cover and who do I call?

Ask for the equipment warranty and the labour warranty as two separate answers. Ask who handles a problem in January, and how fast they come.

Good answer: clear years, a phone number and a named person.
quote: A quote is a plan, not just a price. If two quotes cannot be compared line by line, ask each company to redo them.

quiz.title: Quick quiz: can you spot a good quote?
quiz.intro: Five questions. Tap an answer to see why.

qs.q: In Ontario's heat pump stream, when do you need written pre-approval?
qs.why: Before the install. Ontario's requirements ask for written pre-approval before work starts, so you cannot apply afterward.

qs.q: In BC, how long after the invoice do you have to apply for the BC Hydro heat pump rebate?
qs.why: Six months from the invoice, according to BC Hydro's rebate page.

qs.q: Which is the best sign when an installer talks about sizing?
options: They show heat loss math for your home
They use the size of your old furnace
qs.why: Programs size by how much heat your home loses, not by what was there before. An oversized unit can cost more and run worse.

qs.q: What should be on the quote besides price?
qs.why: Model numbers let you check the qualified list and compare quotes fairly.

qs.q: How many quotes should you get?
qs.why: Three shows you the real range in price, equipment and approach.

messages: Good start. Skim the nine questions again before you call anyone.
Nice. You know more than most buyers.
Perfect score. You are ready to get quotes.

faq: How many installers should I call?
Three is a good number. It shows the real range in price and plan without taking over your month.
Is the cheapest quote the best?
Not always. A low quote can leave out electrical work, a qualified model or the rebate paperwork. Compare the same list of items in each.
How do I check an installer is registered for a rebate?
Use the program's own list. For BC, Better Homes BC publishes registered contractors. For Ontario, use the Home Renovation Savings program pages.
Many installers ask for one. Get the amount and the steps in writing, and check your province's rules on deposits before you pay.
